study_identification.title: Microstructural mapping of neural pathways in Alzheimer’s disease using macrostructure-informed normative tractometry

study_characteristics.study_objective: To propose a novel macrostructure-informed normative tractometry (MINT) framework to investigate how white matter (WM) microstructure and macrostructure are jointly altered in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia, and to compare MINT-derived metrics with univariate diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Denoising using local PCA, Gibbs ringing removal, susceptibility-induced distortion, eddy current, and motion correction, bias field inhomogeneity correction. Bundles with fewer than 96 streamlines were removed.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization was used to remove site effects. Age and sex were modeled as covariates. ComBat parameters were estimated on the training set (CN subjects) and applied to the test set.

response_variable.answer: FA, MD, RD, AxD, and shape of white matter tracts

predictor_effects.answer: Diagnosis, age, and sex were modeled as fixed effects. Cohort was modeled as a random effect in the merged analysis.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study explicitly addresses site effects, a major source of nuisance variance, by using ComBat harmonization. It also models age and sex as covariates, accounting for their potential confounding effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Along-tract bundle profiles for all nine features were harmonized using ComBat using the bundle-wise approach described in Chandio et al. 15 ComBat is a ‘location and scale’ model, where we assume that each measurement is affected by the additive and multiplicative effects of the scanner and protocol, 15,53 estimated using an empirical Bayes method. Covariates can also be specified in ComBat to preserve the known biological variability across subjects (eg, age and sex). In this study, ComBat was run for each of the 30 bundles and nine features, by pooling information across 100 segments of each bundle, with age and sex modeled as covariates.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not describe any validation of the normative model on a non-independent subset of the training data (e.g., using cross-validation within the training set).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study used a split-sample approach, where the normative model was trained on a subset of the healthy controls and then tested on a separate, independent set of healthy controls, as well as the clinical groups.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: For both the ADNI and NIMHANS datasets, data from the CN participants were split into independent subsets of size 35%/15%/50% for training/validation/testing. Data from participants with MCI or dementia were concatenated with the 50% CN subjects to create the test set.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The model was pre-trained on the TractoInferno dataset and then fine-tuned and evaluated on two different datasets (ADNI and NIMHANS), which have different demographics and were acquired with different scanners and protocols. This constitutes a different domain validation.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: In total, we analyzed diffusion data of 1032 subjects from two cohorts - 730 participants from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) Phase 3 collected using seven acquisition protocols and an independent sample of 302 Indian-ancestry participants, evaluated andscannedattwoscannersattheNational Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS) in Bangalore, India... The pretraining dataset consisted of 198 single-shell dMRI volumes already preprocessed from the publicly available TractoInferno training dataset, 38 acquired on 3T scanners with b -values around 1000 s/mm 2 from six studies.

clinical_groups_sex.answer: ADNI MCI/Dementia: 47.81% M; NIMHANS MCI/Dementia: 58.61% M

deviation_metric.answer: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from the normative model for shape, FA, MD, RD, and AxD.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear regression was used to assess the association between diffusion metrics and diagnosis (MCI and dementia vs. CN). Partial Spearman rank-order correlation was used to assess the association between diffusion measures and clinical scores (CDRsb, ADAS13, MMSE for ADNI; NNB-E for NIMHANS), controlling for age and sex.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The MINT framework, by jointly modeling tract shape and microstructure, can disentangle and better interpret the effects of degenerative disease on the brain’s neural pathways, showing consistent patterns of microstructural and macrostructural anomalies in MCI and dementia across two diverse cohorts.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Widespread diffusivity abnormalities were found in MCI and dementia compared to healthy controls, with larger effects in the posterior-temporal region and corpus callosum. Diffusivity patterns from MINT aligned with univariate DTI measures and showed a stronger association with clinical metrics of episodic memory. MINT helps to distinguish microstructural changes from macrostructural alterations, especially for FA, which is susceptible to fiber crossings.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study acknowledges limitations of DTI-based metrics (FA, RD, AxD) in characterizing WM microstructure due to crossing fibers. Tractography and bundle segmentation methods have limitations, including the potential for false positives and difficulties in reconstructing certain bundles (e.g., fornix, cingulum). The sample sizes for the two cohorts were different, which might have influenced the statistical power and the results. Cognitive assessments were not harmonized across cohorts.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The MINT framework provides a novel way to analyze dMRI data by jointly modeling microstructure and macrostructure, which can lead to new insights into how brain WM pathways are altered in neurodegenerative diseases. The use of a pre-trained model (on TractoInferno) and transfer learning makes the approach more efficient.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper uses a novel deep learning framework called MINT (Macrostructure-informed Normative Tractometry) to analyze diffusion MRI data. The study is well-designed, with a large sample size from two different cohorts, and uses appropriate statistical methods for harmonization and analysis. The findings are consistent with previous studies and provide new insights into the joint contribution of microstructural and macrostructural alterations in Alzheimer's disease.
